claim.claim-text: 1. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method of treating or preventing hyperammonemia, by systemic non-oral administration to a subject.

2. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to claim 1, wherein the hyperammonemia arises due to a urea cycle disorder (UCD), glutamine synthetase deficiency, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, organ failure, acute liver failure, hepatic encephalopathy, liver cirrhosis, and/or kidney dysfunction.

3. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to claim 1 or claim 2 wherein the glutamine synthetase protein comprises an amino acid sequence that is at least 90% identical to the amino acid sequence set forth in SEQ ID NO. 1, or is an enzymatically-active fragment thereof.

4. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the glutamine synthetase protein is a fusion protein comprising i) glutamine synthetase; and ii) a peptide comprising a) the sequence HHHHHH (6xHis) and b) a linker comprising 2-10 amino acids, wherein the glutamine synthetase of i) has the sequence of SEQ ID NO. 1 or a variant thereof having glutamine synthetase activity and at least 90% sequence identity to the sequence of SEQ ID NO. 1.
5. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to 4, wherein the linker comprises the sequence GGGGS.

6. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to 4 or 5, wherein the glutamine synthetase protein i) consists of the sequence of SEQ ID NO. 4; or ii) comprises the sequence of SEQ ID NO. 4 with one amino acid deletion; or iii) is encoded by the sequence of SEQ ID NO. 5.

7. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to claims 4 or 5, wherein the glutamine synthetase protein i) consists of the sequence of SEQ ID NO. 4; or ii) is encoded by the sequence of SEQ ID NO. 5.

8. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein the glutamine synthetase protein is in the form of a pharmaceutical composition or a parenteral nutrition composition.

9. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein the GS protein is in a form suitable for parenteral administration or subcutaneous administration to the subject.

10. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to any one of claims 1 to 9, wherein the glutamine synthetase protein is linked to a moiety, preferably wherein the moiety is selected from a protein, a peptide, a non-protein polymer or an affinity tag.
11. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to claim 10, wherein the moiety is polyethylene glycol (PEG), preferably 20kDa N terminal aldehyde PEG.
12. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to claim 11, wherein the PEG is linked to the glutamine synthetase protein at the N terminus of the protein.
13. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to any one of the preceding claims, wherein the glutamine synthetase protein is in monomeric form or is in multimeric form.

14. A glutamine synthetase protein for use in a method according to any one of the preceding claims, wherein the protein is for use in combination with an ammonia lowering agent, preferably wherein the ammonia lowering agent is a nitrogen scavenger; preferably wherein the nitrogen scavenger is selected from the group consisting of: a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of phenylacetic acid or a pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of phenylbutyric acid pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, glycerol phenylbutyrate pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of benzoic acid or a pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, and ammonia binding resin.

15. A glutamine synthetase protein and an ammonia lowering agent for use in a method of treating or preventing hyperammonemia, preferably wherein the glutamine synthetase protein comprises an amino acid sequence that is at least 90% identical to the amino acid sequence set forth in SEQ ID NO. 1, or is an enzymatically-active fragment thereof; and preferably wherein the ammonia lowering agent is a nitrogen scavenger; preferably wherein the nitrogen scavenger is selected from the group consisting of: a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of phenylacetic acid or a pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of phenylbutyric acid pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, glycerol phenylbutyrate pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, a pharmaceutically acceptable salt of benzoic acid or a pharmaceutically acceptable pro-drug thereof, and ammonia binding resin.
